task_instance: Given a sample Q4 budget-vs-actual dataset (two revenue lines with unit/price detail, plus five OpEx lines across the skill's spend categories), perform the skill's core workflow: price/volume decomposition on revenue lines, materiality threshold flagging (10% or $5,000 per the skill's Actual-vs-Budget framework), narrative generation using the skill's required narrative structure (Driver/Outlook/Action) for each material variance, and a text-based waterfall chart with bridge reconciliation table showing Budget -> Actual.
evidence: Created /tmp/.../budget_vs_actual_q4.csv as sample input (2 revenue lines with units/price, 5 opex lines). Wrote and ran variance_analysis.py which: (1) computes Volume Effect = (Actual Units - Budget Units) x Budget Price and Price Effect = (Actual Price - Budget Price) x Actual Units per the skill's price/volume formula, and verifies Volume+Price=Total for each revenue line (both showed 'OK'); (2) flags material variances against the skill's 10%/$5,000 Actual-vs-Budget threshold; (3) generates a narrative per material line item following the skill's exact Driver/Outlook/Action structure; (4) builds a text-based waterfall (per the skill's 'Text-Based Waterfall Format' when no charting tool is available) from Budget Net Result ($321,000) to Actual Net Result ($301,200) via each line's variance as a driver, plus a Bridge Reconciliation Table with %-of-variance and cumulative columns; (5) verifies the waterfall reconciliation (Budget + Sum of drivers = Actual): $321,000 + -$19,800 = $301,200, matches Actual $301,200 -> printed 'OK'. Script output: 'Reconciliation check: OK'. Full deliverable written to variance_report_q4.md (viewed and confirmed all sections present: line item table, decomposition, spend category notes, narratives, waterfall, reconciliation table). No bundled scripts, external services, or connector/MCP tools were required — the skill is a pure methodology/reference document, fully executable with local file and shell tools.
